sampling._note: The pre-fix run sampled the shipping profile over 19 measured documents and named the six long real-world documents it excluded as its weakest point. Lifting that exclusion was ATTEMPTED here and did not succeed within budget. The scope is therefore the same as the pre-fix run, which at least makes the two directly comparable.
sampling.measured_at_shipping_profile: 19 documents -- the 16 synthetic plus y03, y10, y13. Same scope as the pre-fix run, so the two files compare like for like.

not_measured_at_shipping_profile.honest_caveat: Seven of 26 measurable documents, and they carry most of the corpus's pages. The shipping-profile row in this file therefore still rests on 19 documents and must not be quoted as corpus-wide. All seven ARE measured at the candidate profile, where the corpus is complete but for y06.

sampling.what_was_attempted: A six-document extension (y01, y02, y08, y09, y12, y17 -- 571 source pages) was queued to run after the pre-fix sample was reproduced. It was sized from the observed refine3 rate on the batches that had completed: 16 documents / 32 pages in 99 s and 3 documents / 113 pages in 342 s, a steady ~3.0 s per source page, which put the extension at about 29 minutes.
sampling.why_that_estimate_was_wrong: It assumed refine3 cost is linear in SOURCE pages. It is not. The first extension batch (y01 + y02, 194 source pages, predicted ~10 minutes) ran several times longer and was still in its candidate arm at cutoff. refine3 renders and re-measures the OUTPUT three times per arm, and these documents still produce large outputs (y01 +29, y02 +61 excess pages at the candidate profile), so the per-page rate measured on 1-4 page synthetic documents does not transfer. The extrapolation was mine and it was wrong; it is recorded rather than quietly dropped.

y02_nist_sp800171r2.pdf.status: NOW MEASURED. Pre-fix it was OOM-killed twice and its PDFium output rendered to 615 pages against PyMuPDF's 173. It now completes normally at page_err +61 against a reference +59, with word recall matching the reference (0.189 vs 0.191).

exactly_what_happened.shipping_profile: ABORTED BY THE OPERATOR, exit 143 -- not an observed OOM. It had already run far past the ~3.0 s/source-page rate every other refine3 batch held to, and it had already OOM-killed at the cheaper candidate profile in this same post-fix tree, so it was stopped to let the six-document sample extension run. Recorded as an abort rather than a failure because the two are not the same evidence.

Pre-fix PDFium was 576. The inflation on THIS document is essentially untouched (about 1%), which is why scoring still exhausts 15.6 GB.
